PullRequest.Body:

Reverts ad0f100a29aaf8a1880b23c41fc70dffe0fb0349 (#341958) on `release/1.143`.

Removes the sandbox masked environment variable setting, its schema and SDK forwarding, and the associated test coverage. Existing sandbox authentication settings remain unchanged.

The conflict in `copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts` was resolved by preserving the newer slow-managed-settings test and removing only the environment-credentials test introduced by the reverted commit.

### Validation

Validation was run on the release-based revert. The final branch's content was verified identical to the already-built and linted changes before running the tests.

- `npm run build-fast` (VS Code Build Fast task) - passed.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\sandboxConfigForSdk.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentSession.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\preferences\test\browser\settingsTreeModels.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\terminalContrib\chatAgentTools\test\browser\agentHostSandboxForwarder.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\terminalContrib\chatAgentTools\test\common\terminalChatAgentToolsConfiguration.test.ts --reporter dot` - passed, 1,561 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\platform\agentHost\common\sandboxConfigSchema.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\node\copilot\sandboxConfigForSdk.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentSession.test.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\sandboxConfigForSdk.test.ts src\vs\platform\sandbox\common\settings.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\preferences\browser\settingsTreeModels.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\preferences\test\browser\settingsTreeModels.test.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\terminalContrib\chatAgentTools\common\sandboxSettingsReader.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\terminalContrib\chatAgentTools\common\terminalChatAgentToolsConfiguration.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\terminalContrib\chatAgentTools\test\browser\agentHostSandboxForwarder.test.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\terminalContrib\chatAgentTools\test\common\terminalChatAgentToolsConfiguration.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --cached --check` - passed before committing.

Full type-check, integration tests, and interactive UI testing were not run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup, agent-host connection, and sandbox setting changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The forwarder synchronously reads the desired settings and enqueues RootConfigChanged when a host advertises the schema; connection establishment itself does not await this propagation. Configuration-change handling similarly dispatches synchronously but has no added asynchronous prerequisite.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch RootConfigChanged with the sandbox configuration to each connected local or remote agent host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one dispatch per live connection on initial schema availability when state differs, and one per live connection for a relevant settings change when desired state differs
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-connection dispatch existed and additionally carried the masked-environment-variable object; changes to that setting could trigger another fan-out. The diff removes that trigger and payload field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The dispatch enqueue runs synchronously in the connection/configuration event, but is not awaited as part of host connection establishment

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously connected local/remote agent hosts; the settings read is over a fixed mapping that is one entry smaller after the diff
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Connections are visited serially in a synchronous loop; there is no added parallel burst or queue. Initial pushes remain deduplicated by the _scheduled map.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The desired configuration is computed once and cached until a relevant configuration event. Cold computation performs one configuration inspection per fixed mapped key; warm pushes reuse the object. The diff removes one key and its invalidation trigger.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the removed SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS and mapping entries directly eliminate one read, payload member, and event trigger; no replacement path is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual users usually have few connected hosts, but cardinality and scheduling are explicit in the implementation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: startup/configuration work and IPC payload can only stay equal or decrease.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a Copilot agent session with sandboxing enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After SDK create/resume, finalization awaits script-safety configuration and then one sandbox options.update RPC before the session wrapper becomes available. The diff only removes the credentials member from the object sent by this existing RPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or resume the SDK session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful create or resume attempt per launch, with existing fallback attempts only on the documented resume failures
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for session launch, but its call count and inputs are not changed by this diff

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC during successful launch finalization
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same RPC was made and could serialize the configured environment-variable map; after the diff the payload omits that map.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of launched sessions and, before the diff, configured environment-variable entries/host strings; after the diff that variable-sized field is absent
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Launch finalization awaits the RPC sequentially per session; the diff does not add cross-session concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache controls the launch RPC. Sandbox policy construction remains local and bounded by existing filesystem/network policy collections; the removed credential map is no longer copied into the SDK object.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed object spread was the only forwarding point and is deleted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Credential maps could vary in size, but omission cannot increase launch cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: launch boundary count is unchanged and serialization/allocation is reduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start a normal agent turn or /fleet turn and synchronize live sandbox configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every turn awaits the existing sequenced sandbox options.update RPC and then awaited host-support diagnostics before the agent loop starts. Certificate diagnostics begin in the background and are not joined by updateDiagnostics. The removed credential field does not add any operation or move one onto this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing RPC per prepared turn, plus existing explicit configuration/grant updates; calls are serialized per session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same RPC occurred and included the variable-sized credentials object when configured; after the diff it sends a smaller object.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query sandbox host support for diagnostics
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing getHostSupport query after each successful enabled sandbox update
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by sandbox update and therefore on turn preflight; unaffected by the removed field

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check certificate relevance, installation support, and status
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight/completed check per runtime and effective auth/credential cache key; installation-support lookup is separately reused
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Credential-map changes could create distinct cached checks. With credentials omitted, keys coalesce by the remaining auth values, so check cardinality cannot increase.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Started by certificate diagnostics but not awaited by turn updateDiagnostics

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Turn count per live session and, before the diff, unique credential configurations and map size
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sandbox updates use a per-session sequencer. Certificate checks coalesce through a per-runtime promise map, and mutations use a per-RPC SequencerByKey. The diff adds no burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Certificate status caches successes and failures by runtime/config key. Removing credentials reduces possible key cardinality; no cold or negative-cache path is defeated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call flow from _prepareSdkTurn through applyConfig is explicit, and the diff only deletes data from the pre-existing config.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK RPC duration is runtime-dependent, but boundary count and payload direction are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: critical-path RPC count is unchanged, payload allocation is reduced, and certificate-cache cardinality may decrease.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or search the Settings UI for sandbox configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Settings registration and display-name formatting are local synchronous schema/model work. The diff removes one schema entry and one formatting branch; it does not add rendering, layout, filesystem, IPC, subprocess, database, or network work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered settings and settings rows; both decrease by one for this feature
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Local synchronous model/render preparation only; no queue or fan-out introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache behavior was found on this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the only UI changes are deletions of the setting registration, display label, and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The saved UI work is small, but its direction is unambiguously non-regressive.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the Settings UI has less schema and row work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and relevant launch, per-turn, diagnostics, settings-forwarding, IPC, and cache call paths. The revert removes a variable-sized configuration field, one settings event trigger, and associated schema/UI work while preserving existing boundary cardinality; no actionable performance regression or separately evidenced shipped-regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
